result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say the table already works and keep every price, unit and minimum order. A changes nothing visually: it moves the inline styles into classes and makes a few wording edits, and it sensibly flags the past effective date and the risk that email clients strip <style> blocks. However, it assumes a year in the caption. B makes more changes than a light tidy needs: it adds a scroll wrapper with ARIA attributes and increases row padding, which alters the look of the table. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A and B both rightly call the table good, but both still rewrite it, moving the inline styles into classes and renaming the 'Min. order' header. A also increases the padding and adds a scrolling wrapper, while keeping the prices, units, minimum orders and caption wording unchanged. B renames two headers and rewrites the caption with an assumed year of 2026; it flags that assumption, but it is still invented content, so A is slightly better.
